title: HAL: Hardware-assisted Load Balancing for Energy-efficient SNIC-Host Cooperative Computing
problem: SmartNIC processors only improve system-wide energy efficiency at low packet rates when compared to host processors with accelerators (e.g., Intel Xeon with QuickAssist), while host accelerators with more powerful memory subsystems can outperform SNIC accelerators. This limits SNIC value proposition for datacenter deployments requiring high throughput with tail latency constraints.
motivation: As accelerators increasingly integrate into both dedicated SNIC platforms and server CPUs, determining the optimal placement of network function acceleration becomes critical for datacenter energy efficiency and cost-effectiveness.
method: HAL adds a load balancer to the SNIC (a processor on the network interface card) that continuously monitors packet arrival rates and how efficiently the SNIC is working. When the SNIC reaches its efficiency limit at higher packet rates, HAL rate-limits packets to the SNIC and routes excess traffic to the host processor—a more powerful general-purpose CPU with better memory systems. The system was implemented using a commodity FPGA and NVIDIA BlueField-2 SNIC in a standard server and tested on 10 popular network functions.
key_novelty: HAL implements dynamic hardware-based load balancing in the SNIC that monitors real-time efficiency and routes network functions between the SNIC and host processor, enabling high energy efficiency across all packet rates.
contributions: Comparative analysis showing host CPU accelerators with powerful memory subsystems can outperform SNIC accelerators at high packet rates under tail latency constraints
HAL hardware load balancer with intelligent packet rate limiting policy for achieving SNIC-host processor cooperation
Implementation and evaluation on 10 network functions demonstrating 31% system-wide energy efficiency improvement and 10% throughput improvement without increasing tail latency
baselines: Intel Xeon with QuickAssist Technology accelerators
primary_theme: Dynamic load balancing for SNIC-host energy efficiency
